goal: Deliver an ASP.NET Core minimal-API URL shortener that creates short links (optional custom alias and expiry), redirects them, records per-link click analytics, lets owners deactivate links, rate limits link creation per client, and rejects unsafe or private-network target URLs.

functional.text: Create a short link via POST /api/urls with a target URL, optional custom alias and optional expiry. The response includes the short code and an owner token.
acceptance: POST /api/urls with a valid http(s) URL returns 201 with a JSON body containing code, shortUrl, expiresAt (nullable) and ownerToken.
Generated codes are 7 characters of [A-Za-z0-9] and are unique across links.
A missing or malformed url field returns 400 with a problem-details body.
The response Location header points to GET /api/urls/{code}.

functional.text: Allow an optional custom alias used as the short code.
acceptance: POST /api/urls with alias 'my-link' returns 201 and code equals 'my-link'.
An alias already in use returns 409.
An alias outside 3-32 characters or containing characters other than [A-Za-z0-9_-] returns 400.
Aliases are compared case-sensitively.

functional.text: Redirect GET /r/{code} to the target URL for active, unexpired links.
acceptance: GET /r/{code} for an active link returns 302 with Location equal to the target URL.
GET /r/{code} for an unknown code returns 404.
GET /r/{code} for an expired link returns 410.
GET /r/{code} for a deactivated link returns 410.

functional.text: Support optional expiry on links, supplied as an absolute UTC timestamp at creation.
acceptance: POST /api/urls with expiresAt in the past returns 400.
A link with expiresAt in the future redirects with 302 until that time and returns 410 afterwards.
A link created without expiresAt never expires.
GET /api/urls/{code} returns expiresAt and an isExpired flag.
GET /api/urls/{code} returns 200 with code, targetUrl, createdAt, expiresAt and isActive.
The response never includes the owner token.
An unknown code returns 404.

functional.text: Record each successful redirect and expose analytics via GET /api/urls/{code}/analytics.
acceptance: After N successful redirects, GET /api/urls/{code}/analytics returns 200 with totalClicks equal to N.
Responses with 404 or 410 do not increment totalClicks.
The response includes lastClickAt (nullable) and clicks per UTC day.
An unknown code returns 404.

functional.text: Let the owner deactivate a link using the owner token returned at creation.
acceptance: DELETE /api/urls/{code} with the correct owner token in an Authorization bearer header returns 204.
After deactivation, GET /r/{code} returns 410 and GET /api/urls/{code} shows isActive=false.
A missing or wrong token returns 401 or 403 and leaves the link active.
DELETE on an unknown code returns 404.

functional.text: Rate limit POST /api/urls per client, identified by the remote IP address.
acceptance: The 11th creation request from one IP within 60 seconds returns 429 with a Retry-After header.
Requests from a different IP are not affected by another IP's limit.
After the window elapses, creation succeeds again.
GET /r/{code} is not subject to the creation limit.

functional.text: Reject unsafe target URLs at creation.
acceptance: A URL with a scheme other than http or https (for example javascript:, file:, ftp:) returns 400.
A URL containing userinfo credentials (http://user:pass@host) returns 400.
URLs whose host is localhost, a loopback, private (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16), link-local (169.254/16) or IPv6 unique-local/loopback address return 400.
A URL longer than 2048 characters returns 400.

nonFunctional: GET /r/{code} p95 server-side latency under 50 ms at 200 requests/second with in-memory storage.
Short code generation uses a cryptographically secure random source.
Owner tokens are at least 128 bits of entropy and are stored only as a hash.
Unit/integration test line coverage of at least 80% for src/UrlShortener.Api.
Concurrent click recording is thread-safe: 1000 parallel redirects yield totalClicks of exactly 1000.
assumptions: Assumed (no answer): Owner is identified by a random opaque owner token returned once at creation and sent as a bearer token on DELETE; there are no user accounts.
Assumed (no answer): Client for rate limiting is the remote IP address; the limit is 10 link creations per 60 seconds per IP (fixed window), configurable.
Assumed (no answer): In-memory storage is acceptable; data is lost on restart, behind a repository abstraction so a durable database can be added later.
Assumed: Redirect uses HTTP 302 so that clicks are always counted and expiry or deactivation takes effect.
Assumed: Hostnames are checked for private/loopback addresses by literal IP and the name 'localhost'; DNS resolution of hostnames at creation is out of scope.
Assumed: Expiry is an absolute UTC timestamp (expiresAt); relative TTL is not supported.
Assumed: Analytics are aggregate counts only; no IP, user agent or other personal data is stored per click.
Assumed: Extending expiry, audit logging and un-deactivating links are out of scope for this iteration.
